title: Vehicle_data (receding-horizon VGA snapshot)
description: One element of a `vehicle_data_list` array as consumed by `DARP::Vehicle_data::JSON_deserialize`. The parent instance must use `problem: fleet-sizing`. Required non-null `current_plan` is a single object matching `vehicle_plan.schema.json` (cost, vehicle, departure_time, arrival_time, actions); vehicle references are resolved from the parent `fleet_sizing_vehicles`, `virtual_vehicle`, or instance vehicles. Onboard pickup `ActionData` rows must exist in the parallel `vehicle_actions[vehicle_index]` array.

vehicle_index.description: Fleet vehicle index; must match `Vehicle<N>::get_index()` for `instance.get_vehicles().at(vehicle_index)`.

actual_plan_departure_time.description: Seconds; plan departure at materialization (receding horizon); must equal the value used when constructing `Vehicle_data`.

onboard_request_indices.description: Request indices (same convention as `Request::get_index()` / `instance.get_requests().at(i)` ordering used by your instance). Each entry must have a matching pickup `ActionData` in `vehicle_actions[vehicle_index]`.

current_plan.description: Rolling plan for this vehicle, same shape as one element of a solution `plans` array. The C++ loader resolves its vehicle reference from the parent vehicle context; it does not create vehicles from this object. Depot timetable rows are not supported in plan JSON deserialization.

next_location_index.description: Graph node index for discrete location; resolved via a caller-built map (e.g. DM canonical nodes). Omitted or `null`: leave next location unset.

time_at_next_location.description: Seconds to reach `next_location_index` from the receding-horizon clock; if omitted when `next_location_index` is set, only the next node is stored (no time).
